purpose: Clean-room architectural and migration evidence for EmberLights Skins Platform V2.

sources.title: Skin SDK
observations: Skin source uses an XML root with declared dimensions and metadata.
Visual elements and containers are represented as XML children.
Referenced graphics and preview metadata are part of the documented skin model.

sources.title: Interface Settings
observations: Users can select installed interfaces/skins and view metadata/previews.
The application offers an export/edit path for a selected skin.

sources.title: Custom Buttons
observations: Users assign actions through categorized, described, auto-filled editing UI.
Buttons can have labels and multiple assigned action presets.

sources.title: Pads Editor
observations: Pad pages can be created, hidden, favorited, edited, and deleted.
Pads support ordinary/shift and documented pressure/color behavior.
Pages can expose parameters and menus.
Documented layouts support 8-pad and 16-pad modes with shift variants.

sources.title: VDJScript
observations: The same action language is used by skins, keyboard shortcuts, and controller mappings.
The language supports simple commands and compound macros.
emberUses: optional expert text over canonical IR

sources.title: List of VDJScript verbs
observations: A broad documented action catalog feeds editor and mapping workflows.

sources.title: Controller Developers
observations: Controller definition and action mapping are separate files.
Definition names physical MIDI/HID zones; mapping associates those names with actions.
emberUses: separate logical device definition and mapping profile

sources.title: Controller Mapping File v8
observations: Mapper XML identifies a device/version and maps named controls to VDJScript actions.

sources.title: MIDI Controller Definition
observations: Definition XML can describe buttons, sliders, high-resolution values, encoders, LEDs, colors, displays, SysEx, matching metadata, and pad geometry.

globalRules: Source files remain immutable and are never executed.
Every parsed item receives a source pointer, adapter/rule version, status, diagnostic, and proposed target.
Unknown action or visual semantics remain opaque or unsupported.
Responsive conversion is classified separately from exact source geometry parsing.
User-owned assets require provenance and license review before redistribution.
CI uses synthetic or explicitly redistributable fixtures only.
